text.p: Finnish forest industry group Enso Oy said in a statement on Monday it expected its earnings in 1997 to match 1996 when its profit after financial items was 1.67 billion markka.

"The result for the year as a whole is expected to be about the same as in 1996," Enso said. "Enso expects its sales volumes to be higher than last year, but prices will improve only slowly from their present low levels," it added.
"Financial results for the early part of the year will be poorer than for the same period in 1996 because of the low market prices," it said.
Enso said the outlook for its most important business areas was improving.
"Paper consumption is rising, and this will stimulate demand and raise capacity utilisation rates at the mills," it said.
"Despite the increase in orders for paper products, price rises are likely to be slow in coming, as chemical pulp stocks were still above normal at the start of the year," it said.
New capacity would boost supply particularly in coated fine papers this year, it said.
"The trend in costs is expected to be moderate," it said.
